security_audit.summary: The static matches are mostly false positives caused by Markdown backticks, shell examples, placeholder certificate names, and secret-reference documentation. The skill still presents operational risk because it permits broad cluster discovery and mentions agent-directed operator installation, which require explicit authorization and least-privilege controls.

remediation.issue: The skill allows an AI agent to offer a trial and install the mirrord operator after user agreement.
remediation.suggestion: Require a separate explicit confirmation before any cluster change, show the exact commands, and verify namespace, RBAC scope, chart source, and rollback steps.

remediation.issue: Auto-discovery queries workloads, services, CRDs, and resources across all namespaces.
remediation.suggestion: Make discovery opt-in, limit it to named namespaces and resources, use least-privilege RBAC, and redact returned configuration before displaying it.

remediation.issue: Credential and certificate examples could be copied into generated configuration incorrectly.
remediation.suggestion: Keep all credential examples non-secret, require Kubernetes secret references, and warn users not to paste secret values into prompts or generated output.

remediation.issue: Task routing and immediate teardown can affect production work.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend non-production testing, explicit filter review, bounded buffering, and a nonzero drain timeout when in-flight work must be preserved.

content.user_title: Configure Temporal Queue Splitting with mirrord
content.value_statement: Temporal workers need precise task routing during local debugging, but manual Kubernetes configuration is easy to misconfigure. This skill generates resource guidance, filters, validation checks, and troubleshooting steps for mirrord Temporal splitting.
actual_capabilities: Generate MirrordPropertyList guidance for Temporal frontend connections.
Generate MirrordSplitConfig guidance for Temporal worker workloads.
Create message_filter and jq_filter examples for selected tasks.
Explain Helm values, drain timeouts, and buffered task limits.
Validate required fields, namespaces, references, and filter settings.
Troubleshoot operator versions, queue status, and common routing issues.
limitations: It does not apply Kubernetes resources or install Helm releases.
It cannot verify cluster state without authorized kubectl access.
It supports an alpha Team or Enterprise mirrord feature.
It cannot recover work lost through immediate teardown or invalid filters.

use_cases.title: Prepare a local worker session
use_cases.description: Generate the resources and filters needed to route selected Temporal workflows or activities to a developer workstation.

use_cases.title: Configure a shared cluster
use_cases.description: Plan operator settings, workload references, namespaces, secrets, and queue limits for a controlled team environment.

use_cases.title: Diagnose task routing
use_cases.description: Review versions, filters, environment sources, buffering, TLS settings, and queue status when a split behaves unexpectedly.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic split
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up Temporal task queue splitting for my worker. Ask only for the required workload, namespace, queue, and frontend details.

prompt_templates.title: Use a workflow filter
prompt_templates.prompt: Route only Temporal workflows whose IDs start with test-local- to my local worker. Explain the filter and required resource references.

prompt_templates.title: Connect Temporal Cloud
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure Temporal Cloud with TLS and a Kubernetes Secret for the API key. Check namespaces, versions, and secret references before presenting the resources.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose advanced routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Temporal splitting design for filter overlap, jq payload matching, task buffering, drain behavior, TLS configuration, and operator compatibility. Identify risks and propose corrected resources.

output_examples.input: Route workflows beginning with test-local- to my laptop.
output_examples.output: A review-ready split configuration plan with a Temporal queue filter on workflow ID, a matching local target, namespace checks, and a warning that matching tasks are stolen from the deployed worker.

output_examples.input: Connect my self-hosted Temporal frontend with private CA and mTLS.
output_examples.output: A secret-backed connection plan requiring the CA certificate, client certificate, and client key together. It explains that TLS protects the operator connection to the frontend.

output_examples.input: Tasks accumulate while I debug at a breakpoint.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist covering max buffered tasks, filter overlap, drain timeout, worker visibility, and the operator and CLI version requirements.

best_practices: Use Kubernetes Secret references for API keys and certificate material.
Test filters and generated resources in a non-production namespace first.
Review task ownership, buffering limits, drain behavior, and operator versions before starting a session.
anti_patterns: Do not place API keys, certificates, or private keys directly in generated YAML.
Do not use mirror mode or Kafka fields in a Temporal queue configuration.
Do not apply cluster changes automatically without explicit review and authorization.

faq.question: What does this skill configure?
faq.answer: It configures guidance for Temporal queue splitting with MirrordPropertyList, MirrordSplitConfig, mirrord filters, and Helm values.

faq.question: Can it install the mirrord operator?
faq.answer: No. It can explain prerequisites and present commands, but cluster changes require separate explicit review and authorization.

faq.question: How are credentials handled?
faq.answer: Credentials should remain in Kubernetes Secrets and be referenced with secretKeyRef. Do not paste secret values into prompts.

faq.question: Can I route only test workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. Use a message filter on workflow ID or another supported task field, then review overlap and task ownership.

faq.question: Does Temporal support mirror mode here?
faq.answer: No. Temporal splitting is steal-only, so a matching local worker receives the task instead of receiving a copy.

faq.question: Why are tasks delayed during debugging?
faq.answer: The operator buffers matching tasks. Check max_buffered_tasks, filter overlap, drain settings, and the compatibility of the operator and CLI versions.
